mentions.story: Windows XP 2002 for the Itanium: Unbridled rage
mentions.text:
There was also a long piece by a former Intel chip designer who was incredulous about how much the Itanium team was promising numbers based on a very few hand-scheduled routines for FPU-limited code. I think there’s a solid argument that the design just wasn’t based on a correct understanding of what most CPUs did and over-indexed on the most performance-sensitive HPC code. I once helped run some HPC code on a test Itanium system and even there it was just so easy to fall out of the only patterns which performed well and end up slower than older Pentiums even before factoring price into the evaluation.

mentions.author: G3rn0ti
mentions.text:
> to check if your device is running an unmodified windows OS

Remote attestation sounds secure in theory but its Achilles heel is that at the remote end sb will have to perform a judgement of what „an modified OS“ is. And any wrong decision will stress test that sb‘s support division and might be subject to litigation. Likely there will be some industry standard white list which itself might be subject to manipulation (similar to the compromised SSL root certificates we had years ago).

I can’t imagine this will be set in place for all available PC software.

Furthermore, attestation happens during run time of a software stack that might itself be vulnerable to exploits. An attacker might…
